advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the vendor denylist from `rebar.llm.providers` (e.g. registered builder names + `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`) instead of a hardcoded tuple, so a newly supported provider is automatically covered as the docstring/commit claim.
evidence: tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py:20-34: `# Provider ids registered in src/rebar/llm/providers.py ...` followed by `DENYLIST = ( "openai-responses", ... )` — a frozen literal, not read from providers.py

src/rebar/llm/providers.py:46-64: `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` derives provider names dynamically from `known_model_names()` | `_DEPRECATED_PROVIDER_ALIASES` | `_EXTRA_KNOWN_PROVIDERS`; the test duplicates a snapshot of this rather than importing it
ABSENCE: nothing in the test imports from `rebar.llm.providers`, so adding a new builder/provider there cannot update or fail this test — the named guarantee cannot hold
advisory.finding: The vendor-neutrality test's DENYLIST is a hardcoded literal tuple, but its docstring ("the provider tokens ``src/rebar/llm/providers.py`` registers") and the commit message ("a new test sources its denylist from the provider registry so a newly supported provider cannot be named in a skill without the test noticing") claim it is derived from the provider registry. A provider newly added to providers.py will not appear in this static list, so the test silently fails open on exactly the regression it claims to catch.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import the live provider set (builder keys plus `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` / the known-provider frozensets) from `rebar.llm.providers` and build the token set from it, keeping only the hand-maintained model-family aliases (claude/gemini/gpt) as an explicit supplement.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Cover all provider families the registry recognizes (not just OpenAI/Google/Anthropic/Bedrock), or derive the list so the coverage gap cannot open.
evidence: tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py:22-34: DENYLIST contains only openai/google/anthropic/bedrock families
src/rebar/llm/providers.py:61-64: recognized providers are everything `known_model_names()` enumerates (a much larger set) plus the alias frozensets — the DENYLIST is a strict, incomplete subset
advisory.finding: Even as a static snapshot, DENYLIST omits many provider/model families that providers.py' registry recognizes via pydantic-ai's known_model_names() (e.g. groq, mistral, cohere, deepseek, grok/xai, huggingface), so a skill could name one of those vendors and the gate would pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor denylist tokens on word boundaries (e.g. `\b(...)\b`) to avoid substring false positives on short tokens like `gpt`/`openai`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py:36: `_DENY_RE = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(token) for token in DENYLIST), re.IGNORECASE)` — no word boundaries
tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py:55: `match = _DENY_RE.search(line)` — unanchored substring match
advisory.finding: The denylist is matched as a case-insensitive substring (`_DENY_RE.search(line)`), so short tokens like `gpt` and `openai` will match any larger word containing them, risking future false positives in skill prose and making the gate brittle.

evidence: examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md:13-15 now states 'A defect audit, not a tidying pass: deletion-only complexity work belongs to rebar-tidy' and 'Use when the user wants a defect, maintainability or tech-debt review'

docs/documentation-policy.md:13 names the maintained page aligned with implementation as the canonical source for internal documentation

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the denylist from the provider registry (e.g. _pydantic_ai_known_providers() / ProviderSession builders) or add a test asserting DENYLIST covers every registered provider, so a new provider cannot be named in a skill undetected.
evidence: Docstring: 'Both skill trees are scanned for the provider tokens ``src/rebar/llm/providers.py`` registers plus the model families those providers serve'
DENYLIST is a static tuple of string literals (lines 22-34) with no import from rebar.llm.providers

src/rebar/llm/providers.py:104-117 registers builders dynamically ('anthropic','bedrock','openai','openai-chat') and _pydantic_ai_known_providers() (line 46-64) derives names from pydantic-ai; none of these feed the test
tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:303 shows `_pydantic_ai_known_providers` is importable and usable as a registry source
ABSENCE: no cross-check (e.g. assert DENYLIST covers the registry / _pydantic_ai_known_providers) exists, so adding a new provider id to providers.py leaves the test silently green
advisory.finding: The denylist is a hardcoded literal, not sourced from the provider registry as the docstring/commit claim; a newly registered provider in providers.py will NOT be added automatically, so the specific regression the change exists to catch ('a newly supported provider cannot be named in a skill without the test noticing') is not actually caught.
scenarios: A maintainer adds a new provider (e.g. 'mistral') to providers.py and names it in a skill; the test passes because 'mistral' is not in the frozen DENYLIST
advisory.suggested_fix: Import the registered provider names from rebar.llm.providers (e.g. ProviderSession(...)._builders keys plus _pydantic_ai_known_providers()) and either build DENYLIST from them or assert DENYLIST is a superset, so a new provider id fails the test automatically.

merged_from: test_skill_tree_exists is an existence-only test (a bare `.is_file()` check) with no structural-contract content; it breaks on a rename and adds no behavioral coverage beyond what the scan test's own liveness anchor would provide.
